context.clinical_context_summary: 69-year-old Female with a past medical history of acute kidney failure with cortical necrosis, rhabdomyolysis, and bacteremia (prior sepsis). Presents with FALL. Significant risks include: 1) History of sepsis/bacteremia requires heightened vigilance for infection signs, 2) Chronic kidney disease post-acute cortical necrosis may affect fluid balance and hemodynamic stability, 3) Temperature readings consistently low (34.9-35.1°C mean 35.01°C) strongly suggest axillary/peripheral thermometer use rather than core measurement - interpret fever thresholds accordingly (axillary reads ~0.5-1°C lower than oral), 4) Age and fall presentation warrant monitoring for orthostatic hypotension and occult injury.
context.rationale: Thresholds are personalized based on baseline data and clinical history. HR normal range (55-90) reflects her documented baseline (mean 69, range 57-88); wider warning allows for pain/stress response post-fall. BP thresholds account for her measured range (SBP 97-140, DBP 46-117) with conservative upper limits given renal history and fall risk from hypotension. SpO2 threshold set at 92% normal with 90% warning given one documented low reading (86%) and age-related risk; values up to 100% are acceptable. RR thresholds match her baseline (10.6-21.6). Temperature thresholds are critically adjusted: given consistent readings of 34.9-35.1°C (axillary measurement inferred), normal range is lowered to 34.5-36.5°C with fever concern at >36.5°C axillary (equivalent to ~37.5°C oral). History of bacteremia mandates careful monitoring for even subtle temperature elevations indicating infection recurrence.
